hook_text: The seafront railings are orange. The statue is green. Same sea air, different metals.
clip_script: Mossel Bay seafront. Steel railings flaking orange: rust! Only iron and steel rust, when water and air reach them, and salty sea air makes it faster. Paint, oil or zinc keep it away. The bronze statue is green: that is tarnish, just on the surface. Back in class: a metal spoon in hot water gets hot to the handle. Metals conduct heat. And a magnet? It grabs the steel paper clip but ignores the aluminium can.
visual_style: Whiteboard railing turning orange, a statue turning green, then a spoon glowing red up its handle and a magnet picking objects.
mood: Detective-style, solving three mysteries about metals.
pacing: Two seafront mysteries, then two quick classroom tests.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and test which things in your home a magnet picks up.
